summary.title: The Reverse Interview: How To Choose Your Next Company
summary.one_liner: A reverse interview flips the usual power imbalance so you can gather real information about a company, role, and team before accepting a job offer.
keywords: how to evaluate a job offer
questions to ask in an interview
takeaways: Interviews favor the company: candidates have limited time and less information, so take control by asking specific, context-driven questions.
Evaluate company, team, and role together, and weigh them differently by company stage; early-stage companies make company and team more critical.
Ask about how things work in practice (for example, decisions made autonomously or recent team changes) rather than scripted questions like 'what is the culture?'.
Dig deeper with follow-up prompts, recast what you heard back to the interviewer, and back-channel with former employees or the hiring manager.
Optimize for long-term career impact over short-term title or salary, since company growth strongly shapes future opportunities.
summary.summary: The article, co-written by Reforge partners Elena Verna and Crystal Widjaja with contributions from other Reforge leaders, argues that job interviews are weighted toward the employer and that candidates need a structured reverse interview to counter this. It lays out a five-step process: self-assessment, deciding what you want, identifying fitting companies, filtering using insider contacts, and coming better prepared than the interviewer. It supplies sample questions across culture, scope, team structure, role history, and company perception of the candidate, plus tactics for going beyond scripted answers, handling unanswered questions, and asking for more time. Personal anecdotes from the contributors support the points.
